versions.changelog:
For Jellyfin 12. Fixes for the three open issues.

- Newer OpenAI models work now. They refuse `max_tokens` and only accept the default temperature, so the plugin switches to `max_completion_tokens` and drops the temperature on its own, then remembers it for that model. You can also pick the field in the settings ("Reply length limit field"). Fixes #4.
- You can exclude libraries from AI Search. Ticked libraries are left out of the index, the AI search popup and the AI matches in Jellyfin's search, but still show up in Jellyfin's normal title search. Fixes #3.
- Building the index with a model that gives no embeddings (a reranker, or llama.cpp with `--pooling rank`) now stops with a clear message saying so, instead of a JSON error. If only a few titles fail, the build skips them and tells you how many. Fixes #2.

For Jellyfin 12. Searching is much faster, and you can now see where each result comes from.

What's new:
- Jellyfin's own search no longer waits for AI Search. Title results show up right away.
- AI matches get their own "AI Search" row under Jellyfin's results, with a short reason under each title.
- If a chat model is set up, it writes a one-line reason for each AI match a few seconds later.
- The plugin speaks French or English. By default it follows each user's Jellyfin language, or you can pick one in the settings.
- The search model is loaded as soon as you open the search page, so the first search isn't slow anymore.
- Repeated searches are almost instant, and the AI popup no longer loads your whole library before searching.

Fixes:
- The search page no longer jumps up or down while results and reasons load.
- Opening the AI search button no longer scrolls the page back to the top.
- The search history list in the popup is back to its normal layout.
- Remote search works again for searches made with an API key.
- Search log files no longer start with a byte-order mark.

TV and mobile apps still get AI matches mixed into Jellyfin's results, waiting at most 2 seconds for them. Jellyfin 10.11 servers stay on 1.1.1.0.

For Jellyfin 12. Jellyfin's own search now also finds titles by meaning, shown in the usual Movies, Shows and Episodes rows after the title matches. New options: turn it on or off, only use it for searches that look like a sentence, limit how many matches it adds, hide the AI search button completely (native search only), and keep a log of every search for a few days so an admin or API key can collect them.

name: ShareLinks [✓]
description:
Adds secure, expiring guest-share links for Jellyfin items using temporary hidden users, one-use token redemption, restrictive policies, and scheduled cleanup.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 19:22 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks
overview: Temporary guest links for Jellyfin movies and episodes.

versions.changelog: Fixes shared movies failing with "media could not be found" when an intro plugin like Local Intros is installed (#23). The intros aren't part of the share, so the guest couldn't open them and playback stopped before the movie. Guests now skip intros, and any video or audio a guest can't open is left out of what the server sends them, whichever plugin or endpoint it came from.
Fixes share links on Jellyfin 12 and the ShareLink button missing on new Docker installs.

Fixes redemption on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and later (#19). Jellyfin changed the signature of the method the plugin uses to set a guest's password, so every link failed with a MissingMethodException and the guest landed on the dead-link page. The plugin now picks whichever version of that method the server has, so the same build works on every 10.11 release. Tested on 10.11.8 and 10.11.11.

Guests are now blocked from other plugins' API endpoints on the server, not just hidden from their UI in the browser. A share guest holds a real Jellyfin token, so anything that only hid a button left the endpoint answering it. Jellyfin's own API is untouched: the share tag already limits it to the shared title, and playback needs it. The config page lists your installed plugins with a checkbox each, so you can let one through when it genuinely needs to serve guests, such as an intro skipper. The guest hidden selectors setting is renamed to say what it is: cosmetic, it tidies the view and enforces nothing. Also fixes the dashboard devices page coming up empty after a share expired: deleting a guest left its device row behind, and a device whose user is missing makes Jellyfin fail the whole device listing rather than skip one row.

Fixes a season share exposing the rest of the series: the tag was going onto the season's parent series, and Jellyfin treats a parent's tags as belonging to all of its children, so every other season became visible to the guest. Tagging now only ever goes downwards. Take this update if you have shared a season with a link that is still live. Also in this release: a link can be made multi-use from the create popup so several people can use it until it expires, with a configurable ceiling on how many watch at once (ten by default), and the dashboard gains a "Clean up finished links" button that removes revoked, expired and failed records.

The ShareLink button now sits in its own section at the bottom of the item menu, and only appears for a movie, series, season or episode instead of turning up on things like a cast member. It is properly admin only again: the current user was cached for the whole page, so switching accounts in the same tab could leave the button visible to a normal user (the server always refused them). Share tags are hidden from everyone except admins, on the title and in the tag filter. Security: one-use links can no longer be redeemed twice, the configured maximum expiry is respected, the raw token is dropped from storage when a link dies, the token secret file is 0600, guest accounts can no longer sign in from the login page at all, and the runtime reflection shims around Jellyfin's APIs are gone.

Series and seasons can now be shared, not just single movies and episodes: the share tags the whole tree so the guest can browse and play everything inside it, and cleanup strips it all again. Expired or invalid links now show a friendly page that redirects to the Jellyfin home instead of raw JSON. The guest hidden selectors setting now defaults to empty.

ShareLink button on the item menu, temporary guest users confined by tag policy, expiring links with a date/time picker, admin dashboard with revoke, and a configurable guest lockdown that hides tag/genre/studio/cast links, the add-to-playlist and add-to-collection actions, and other plugins' UI. The creation popup is localized in English and French. Guest sessions are now minted server side: no password is ever stored or sent anywhere, the guest page only carries a session token, and expired guests are cleaned up every 30 minutes.

versions.changelog: Official Release 3.3.7

Official Release 3.3.6

- **BoxSet & Collection Support**: Added Primary, Thumbnail, and Backdrop image resolution for collections across Jellyfin and Emby.
- **Asset Path Resolution**: Resolves Collections directory at root or within subfolders, supporting both nested folders and flat file structures.
- **Smart Name Normalization**: Handles '[boxset]' tag stripping, '&' vs 'and' variants, illegal character sanitization, and automatic 'Collection' suffix matching.
- **Metadata Refresh Detection**: Implemented HasChanged check using file timestamps so library refreshes detect updated assets on disk.
- **Real-Time WebSocket Sync**: Added collection asset handling to automatically invalidate cache and update artwork via WebSocket stream.
- **Opt-In Setting**: Added UpdateCollection configuration toggle (default false) in plugin configuration page.
Official Release 3.3.5

Official Release 3.3.4

- **WebSocket Real-Time Sync**: Added background listener service connecting to `/ws/events` for instant image updates.
- **Direct Image Application**: Streams and persists image updates directly using internal provider APIs upon receiving events.
- **Enhanced Configuration Page**: Added Real-Time Sync toggle, Posterizarr URL input, and API key configuration with live connection test diagnostics.
- **Volume Latency Tolerance**: Added 2-second retry loop for newly created image files.
- **Catalog Image**: Configured `imageUrl` in repository manifests.

Official Release 3.3.3

- **Persistent State Caching**: Added `posterizarr_sync_cache.json` in the plugin data directory to track file sizes, timestamps, and image metadata. Unchanged assets are skipped instantly in memory with zero network I/O.
- **Directory & File Caching**: Added `AssetPathResolver` to cache root library shares and folder file listings. Reduces tens of thousands of remote SMB/NFS round-trips to a single query per media folder.
- **Parallel Async Sync Task**: Upgraded `PosterizarrSyncTask` to use `Parallel.ForEachAsync` with adaptive concurrency, replacing single-threaded sequential processing.
- **Tiered Image Verification**: Added 4KB header and file-length pre-checks to eliminate continuous ~30 MB/s full-file MD5 hash calculations across the network.
- **Debug Mode Toggle**: Debug messages (`[Posterizarr DEBUG]`) are now directly controlled by the plugin's `EnableDebugMode` setting and visible in the Jellyfin log viewer without changing server logging configurations.
- **Emby Optimization**: Added same-path timestamp comparison to prevent double-hashing identical local files in Emby.
- **Performance Benchmark**: Successfully verified on a 39,000-item library, reducing task runtime from **32m 51s to 13 seconds (~151x faster)** with near-zero network and disk utilization.

Official Release 3.3.2

- **Jellyfin 12.0.x & 10.11.x Multi-Targeting**: Compiled for both `.NET 9` (Jellyfin 10.11.x) and `.NET 10` (Jellyfin 12.0.x) with target-specific ABI dependencies (`10.11.0.0` and `12.0.0.0`).
- **Automated Dual Packaging**: Manifest and release pipelines now generate separate distribution archives (`Posterizarr.Plugin_v3.3.2.zip` and `Posterizarr.Plugin_v3.3.2-jf12.zip`).
- **Emby API Token Authentication**: Updated media server logo upload headers to use `MediaBrowser Token="{token}"` format, resolving upload failures on Emby servers.

name: Native Trickplay [✓]
description:
Generates HLS I-frame variants so Apple TV / AVPlayer clients get native
scrubbing thumbnails on the transport bar — no client-side overlay needed.
One-time ffmpeg cost per item, then cached.
Includes a configurable daily prune scheduled task (orphan removal,
age-based eviction, optional LRU size cap) so the cache doesn't grow
unbounded.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 19:22 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HarshLabs/jellyfin-plugin-native-trickplay/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/HarshLabs/jellyfin-plugin-native-trickplay
overview: Native HLS trickplay for AVPlayer-based clients (Apple TV).

versions.changelog: When Jellyfin played a video without converting it, the trickplay playlist could name the wrong video format (for example HEVC for a 10-bit H.264 file), so the Apple TV prepared the wrong decoder and took much longer to start. The playlist now names the format Jellyfin actually sends, including 10-bit H.264 (High 10). No change for HDR or Dolby Vision videos.

Videos whose HEVC stream declares a level above 5.0 (common with certain x265 encodes) were rejected by the Apple TV when served through the trickplay-enabled playlist, and the player fell back to the thumbnail track. The playlist now also offers a level 5.0 entry, the same approach Jellyfin uses for its own playlists, so these videos play normally with scrubbing thumbnails intact. No change for other videos.

- Fixed: trickplay playlists and image segments now enforce each user's library access and parental controls. Previously, any signed-in user could request the scrubbing thumbnails of items outside their allowed libraries.
- Improved: the dashboard's item list loads dramatically faster on large libraries (it no longer reads every cached playlist from disk just to show cache status).
- Improved: changing "Concurrent encodes" now takes effect immediately — no server restart needed.
- Fixed: corrupt video files could make HDR detection time out, producing washed-out thumbnails for HDR content.
- Fixed: searching with an extremely large season or episode number could error the item list.
- Hardened the release pipeline: build steps are now pinned to exact, immutable versions.

After updating, restart your server once as usual. No cache regeneration is required.

If you reinstall Jellyfin (or its database gets rebuilt) and point the plugin back at your existing cache folder, the plugin now relinks every cached entry to your library automatically — no re-encoding, no lost cache.

- New: orphaned cache entries (from a reinstall or database rebuild) are automatically relinked to your items at server startup and before every scheduled prune run.
- New: the dashboard shows a warning banner with a one-click "Relink orphaned entries" button whenever orphaned entries are detected.
- Fixed: Cache Status no longer counts orphaned entries as cached (previously it could show 100% coverage while every item listed as "not cached" and playback re-encoded).
- Fixed: the daily prune task no longer deletes a reinstalled server's still-valid cache — it relinks first and only removes entries that truly match nothing.

Update, restart your server once, and your cache reconnects on its own within about 30 seconds — or press the new Relink button on the plugin dashboard.

Fixes playback stalling on Apple TV when audio is passed through unchanged (stream copy). The playlist could advertise the wrong audio format, which made the player wait forever for audio it was never going to get. If playback ever froze right after turning subtitles off, this is that fix.
Fixed playback breaking on SDR variable-bitrate files when trickplay is enabled. Affected videos could freeze mid-playback or get stuck on a loading screen when resumed; they now play normally.

* On HDR sources, tone mapping now runs on the GPU when your ffmpeg build supports it (OpenCL for Intel QSV / VAAPI / AMD on Linux, CUDA for NVIDIA, Metal on macOS). The previous CPU tone-mapping path was the dominant cost on HDR content — moving it to the GPU is the bulk of the speedup. Falls back to the old CPU path automatically when no GPU tone-mapping filter is available.

* The ffmpeg filter chain now thins frames down to the trickplay rate (one every couple of seconds) before any per-frame work runs. Previously every decoded frame was transferred GPU → CPU before being discarded — for a 2-hour 4K HDR source that's hundreds of thousands of wasted full-resolution transfers.

* New "GPU tone-mapping for HDR" toggle in the plugin settings, on by default. Disable it if GPU tone-mapping misbehaves on your hardware — encodes still benefit from the filter-chain reorder.

* Encodes that hit a GPU tone-mapping issue now fall back to CPU tone-mapping automatically (keeping hardware decode), and only drop to full software decode if the hardware decoder itself fails. The dashboard's hardware-path column shows what's actually in use (e.g. "QSV+OCL", "VideoToolbox+VT") so you can see the path each encode is taking.

A user on an Intel iGPU reported that a 2-hour 4K HDR film took ~90 minutes to generate on the prior version. The same encode finishes in roughly 10 minutes on this version.

Previously, if you deleted a library from Jellyfin, the plugin's
"Find & select items" list and the daily pre-generation task kept
seeing items from the removed library until Jellyfin's next library
scan cleaned them up — which meant inflated totals on the dashboard
and the nightly task wasting time encoding files that were no longer
in any library.

The plugin now scopes its lookups to the libraries currently visible
in Jellyfin, so the moment you remove a library the dashboard total
matches the Cache Status widget and the pre-gen task stops touching
those items.

No action required — just update the plugin and the next dashboard
load will reflect the correct counts.

Avoids advertising an iframe trickplay variant whose playlist resolves
to a valid-but-empty stub on cache miss — that combination can stall
AVPlayer on tvOS 26 with seek-shifted on-demand transcodes. Trickplay
appears on the next playback session once the warmup task generates
the cache.

* Search results above 200 items now load progressively. Default page is 500; 'Load more' appends the next batch and 'Load all' pulls everything matching the current filter.
* New 'Select all N items matching this filter' link appears once you've checked some visible items in a paginated result. Click it to select every match — including items not yet rendered. The bulk Generate or Evict action then operates on the entire match set, not just the page in front of you.
* Selection persists across pagination — checking an item on page 1 stays checked when you load page 2.
* 'Clear selection' link in the banner dismisses an all-matching selection. Filter, sort, or search changes also reset selection automatically.

Cancel active encodings

* New "Cancel" button on each in-flight row in the Encoding-in-progress panel, plus a "Cancel all" button in the footer.
* Works for both queued items (waiting for an encoder slot) and items currently being encoded.
* Existing cached trickplay for the canceled item is preserved — only the in-progress attempt is dropped.
* Cancel is idempotent — a second click is harmless.

Release notes now reflect actual changes per release. Prior versions all showed "Initial release" due to a publishing oversight.

versions.changelog: 10.11.11.0 - Want to watch gains three options, all off by default and all requiring the arrived-titles playlist (contributed by David Rappo, @rappo, in PR 21): the home row can lead with the titles already on your playlist, a title comes off the playlist once it is watched (a series once every episode is played), and a movie or series page gets a bookmark button among its own. Plugin rows are reachable with a TV remote's D-pad. Not interested, off by default, lets each user hide a title from their own Web UI pages without hiding it for anyone else. A user with a parental rating limit sees the Web UI sections narrowed to the titles that limit allows, rather than none of them. The home Discover row, the Want to watch row, and the item page rows each have a placement setting; existing settings carry over. The Gaps Report's toolbar is grouped by what each control acts on, every header has a select-all, a line above the list says how many rows the filters hide, and Add to TODO is now Add to watchlist. The report is usable at phone width, and the settings page has collapsible sections, a search, and better screen reader support. A new scheduled task, Prune gaps from deleted items, takes deleted library items out of the report: a gap they were the only source of is removed, and one with other sources moves to the next. It has no default schedule; it waits for a running scan, and a second scan waits for the first. Recommendation groups link to the owned title they came from. Books get an OpenLibrary id field and albums and artists a Discogs id field in the metadata editor, with a link on the item's page; a dedicated OpenLibrary or Discogs plugin takes over when installed. Links are built from each title's ids when the report loads, so a link plugin installed later applies everywhere. The report takes far less memory and disk (on a library with 83,000 gaps, about 1.6 GB down to 200 MB in memory and 245 MB down to 131 MB on disk), loads in about half the time, and is written far less often during scans and where-to-watch lookups. Existing reports convert on first load; a report saved by this version cannot be read by an earlier one, so going back shows an empty report until its next scan.

10.11.10.0 - The Maintenance section has a Fulfillment queue for an administrator who fetches titles by hand. It folds every user's TODO list into one row per title, sorted by how many people still want it, names who is still waiting, and shows the streaming-service icons as soon as the queue opens, with the same links a TODO row already has. Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. With Everyone's watchlist on (off by default), that same household list is a Discover source and leads the Discover view of every domain it has entries for. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. The report's Send action has a quality profile picker, filled from the stack's own profile list and preselecting the profile you configured, so an older title the default profile cannot find a release for can still be sent. The report's My TODO list popup is gone; the Fulfillment queue is where an administrator sees every list. The report's multi-select bar can Acquire, Request, or Resolve a checked batch (Resolve applies one shared note), alongside Mint and Add to TODO. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. With "Want to watch: move arrived titles into a playlist" on, a title that is in the library moves into that user's own Jellyfin playlist the next time it is verified, so it shows up in every client. The playlist is named Want to Watch unless you change it, and only a real file counts as arrived. Amazon and web-search links for a book or album include the author or artist, on the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue. TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are set with the same chip pickers the other curated sources use. A book's dialog loads its description from OpenLibrary when you open it. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. A library that sets a metadata fetcher order keeps TVmaze in the series check. TVmaze is not a Jellyfin metadata fetcher, so it is always asked and ranked last.

10.11.9.0 - Mind the Gaps now reaches into Jellyfin's own pages through an experimental, opt-in Web UI, with a master switch and one toggle per surface in settings, all off by default. A person's page lists what they made that you do not own, a movie or series page suggests titles like it that you are missing, an artist's page lists the albums you do not have, and a book page or an author's own page lists more by the same author. The home page can show a Discover row of the recommendations your scans found from titles you own and from lists that are public by nature (TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and TMDB's own feeds), never from a watchlist, wantlist, favorites, or a personal list. Click a card for a detail dialog with TMDB's synopsis, genres, runtime, rating, a trailer link, and a link to the title's JustWatch page, then send it to Radarr or Sonarr with the quality profile you pick; the dialog and the card grids can be driven from a keyboard or a TV remote. A user with a parental rating limit is shown none of these sections. With Want to watch turned on, every card carries a bookmark that adds the title to your own list, and the home page can show a Want to watch row of what you have listed and do not yet own. The TODO list is now kept per user, in the plugin's data folder, and removed when the user is deleted; the first administrator to open the old shared list takes it over, and an administrator can switch the report's TODO to everyone's lists to see and manage them. The Gaps Report loads faster: it fetches one tab at a time as slim rows, fetches a row's details only when you open it, revalidates what it already holds instead of downloading it again, and loads its script and stylesheet as separately cached files; the saved report is stored as one file per domain, and an existing report is converted automatically. A row shows up to two streaming-service icons, following your provider and monetization filters and wearing the service's logo (a service TMDB lists as several providers, such as a "with Ads" tier, shows as one icon and one provider filter entry), and clicking them opens the title's TMDB watch page. Gaps left behind by a source you have since removed or turned off are pruned on every scan, and a Prune stale gaps button under Maintenance does it right away. A TMDB list that cannot be read, such as a private one, no longer stops the other lists from being scanned, filling in a large library's series content is done in batches, and the scan log says how long each source took. New, and off by default: the report and the Web UI can load their posters, covers, and streaming-service logos through your server instead of each browser fetching them from TMDB and the other providers. Turn on "Keep the pages' images on this server" in the new Images section of settings; the server fetches each image once, from a fixed list of provider hosts only, keeps it under its cache folder, and sends the browser on to the provider whenever it cannot serve one, and a "Trim the image cache" scheduled task keeps the cache to the size you set (500 MB by default).

10.11.8.0 - The Gaps Report is reorganized around your library's domains: Movies, Shows, Music, and Books are now the primary tabs, each badged with its own gap count, with Set completion, Creator works, and Discover scoped underneath as a view you pick per domain, so only the active domain's data is loaded at a time. A Compact view toggle switches to a denser layout. Click a title to expand its detail in place: the overview, where to watch, and (outside Compact view) every information and action button tile inline instead of opening separate popovers; collapsed, the same actions live behind three icon popovers on the row, and a collapsed title's own browser tooltip shows its overview with no click at all. The toolbar is split into a filter row and an action row, and the settings page is reorganized into one collapsible section per provider (TMDB, Trakt, MDBList, Discogs, OpenLibrary, TheTVDB, IMDb, JustWatch), each badged on or off, with a search box that opens whichever section matches. Four new TMDB feeds, Top Rated, Popular, Upcoming, and Now Playing, can be turned on individually under Discover, and Jellyfin 12.0 is now a supported target alongside 10.11, each release building and shipping its own ABI-matched package. Gaps now show real cover art for books (bibliography and subject lists), music (MusicBrainz discography and artist works), and series completion episodes (TMDB, TheTVDB, and TVmaze all supply a still where they have one) instead of a blank thumbnail, falling back to the placeholder rather than a broken-image icon when a cover fails to load; MDBList entries carry a poster and description like every other source. A creator's page can be trimmed further with a minimum TMDB vote count for a movie credit and a minimum episode count for a TV credit. The TODO list shows an image and release date per entry. Sending a whole-series gap to Sonarr from a filmography, recommendation, or favorites entry sends the series' own title rather than the name of whatever surfaced it, and a rejected Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr request shows the service's validation message instead of a raw response body.

name: Subtitle OCR [✓]
description:
Converts embedded image-based subtitle tracks (VobSub/DVD and PGS/Blu-ray) to external SRT or ASS files using nOCR pattern matching. Pure managed code: no Tesseract and no native libraries, using the ffmpeg your server already ships. The .nocr database format is interchange-compatible with Subtitle Edit, so databases trained or corrected in its GUI drop straight in. A scheduled task scans your Movie and Episode libraries and writes a subtitle file beside each image-based track. OCR text is optionally spell-checked with Hunspell and corrected with Subtitle Edit's OCR fix lists, both fetched on demand.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 19:22 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IDisposable/jellyfin-plugin-subtitleocr/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/IDisposable/jellyfin-plugin-subtitleocr
overview: OCR image-based DVD and Blu-ray subtitles to SRT or ASS

versions.changelog:
Recognition is far more accurate and roughly three times faster. The bundled Latin database carries glyph shapes trained on real disc fonts, so few characters read as the unknown box. A file gives up every subtitle track in one pass rather than one pass per track, tracks recognize in parallel (Max parallelism leaves half the cores to playback), and image buffers are reused, so a run no longer drives the full garbage collections that interrupt playback. The matcher takes the best matching glyph rather than the first the database lists, reads case from the image's own x-height and cap height, splits a merged glyph pair, matches a multi-segment glyph on shape at any size, and follows the line's italic state so a stray mid-word italic reads as the run around it. Whether a track is light text on a dark outline or the reverse is read off the track itself, per track, so the Invert luma setting is gone, and word spacing is calibrated to real disc fonts.
Output keeps more of the disc. ASS carries the color the subtitles were drawn in as its style, with an override only on the lines that differ, places an off-center sign on the full alignment grid, escapes a literal brace, and rounds its timecodes; Auto picks ASS for a track that is positioned or uses more than one color. A cue never ends after the next one begins, a too-short cue is held to a 750 ms readable minimum, and a re-sent duplicate cue merges with its neighbor.
Text correction covers misread digits (a 1 between letters as l or I, a 0 as o), the two-letter words It, Is, In and If, a lowercase l after a speaker label, split contractions and quotes, punctuation spacing, a leading speaker dash, curly quotes, and padded sound-cue brackets. An accented Latin letter foreign to the track's language folds to its base ("Nothing" for "Nothińg"), keeping each language's own accents and leaving cast and character names alone. Spell-check protects names in singular and plural and runs before sentence casing, so a misread at the start of a line resolves against the dictionary instead of freezing into a name. The l-to-I fixes are English-only, so French keeps its elided articles. Language and hearing-impaired detection read a cue's words, not its markup, so close languages like Danish and Norwegian separate, and a track the database cannot really read is discarded rather than shipped.
The extraction log is its own dashboard page, with a Reprocess all button that runs the reprocess task and shows its progress, and a per-row reprocess for a single item. New settings: Fold foreign accents (on), and Aggressive OCR fixes (off) for the riskier digit twins 5/S and 8/B on a poorly scanned disc. The plugin is built against 10.11.0, the target ABI it declares, so it loads on every 10.11 server.

Output format is now selectable: SRT, ASS, or Auto, which decides per track and writes ASS only when a cue sits away from the bottom of the screen (PGS carries the position), so an ordinary track keeps the universally supported format. OCR text is spell-checked with Hunspell, protecting Title-case proper nouns and words drawn from the item's Jellyfin metadata (title, overview, series, cast and character names) so show and character names survive. Subtitle Edit OCR fix replace lists are applied when present; dictionaries and fix lists download on demand and re-download once older than a configurable age. A track with an undetermined language now has one detected from its OCR text and is named accordingly, and the track title, forced, hearing-impaired, and commentary flags appear in the file name so commentary tracks are identifiable. A hearing-impaired track is recognized from its own text when the source flags nothing, which is the norm for a remuxed disc. New OCR corrections cover misread apostrophes in contractions, mid-word capital X, V, and I, optional ellipsis folding, and bogus italic runs around single characters and punctuation. An unread glyph now costs nothing when matching a word against the dictionary, so "batt□e" resolves to "battle" and a damaged name can be restored from the item's metadata. A new "Reprocess extracted subtitles" task re-OCRs every logged file from its source with the current settings. Each file is probed with a single ffprobe pass rather than two, and only one OCR or reprocess task runs at a time.

Detect image-based subtitles by probing every Movie and Episode with ffprobe, since Jellyfin does not store PGS/VobSub streams in its metadata. A per-file cache skips files that are unchanged and were probed within a configurable window, with a force-rescan option. Word spacing now scales with subtitle line height, fixing spaces inserted between every letter on HD Blu-ray text. New options: extract only selected languages, discard a track whose dropped-event ratio is too high (removing any stale SRT), and a filename tag ({name}.{lang}.OCR.srt, shown as the subtitle title) so the plugin only ever overwrites or deletes its own output. A config-page modal lists every extracted file with a link to its movie or episode. The scheduled task now sits under its own category.

Initial production release. OCRs embedded image-based subtitles (VobSub/DVD and PGS/Blu-ray) to SRT files using nOCR pattern matching, with Subtitle Edit-compatible .nocr databases. Pure managed code: no Tesseract, no native dependencies. Optionally skips image tracks whose language already has a text subtitle.

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

versions.changelog:
v3.0.1.2 - Discovery background work respects its master switch, Trakt travels with backup

- Seerr discovery generation and the Trakt refresh no longer run while Discovery user access is off; stored choices resume automatically on re-enabling
- Backup export/import round-trips the "Enable Trakt discovery" flag, so the choice survives a move to a fresh installation
- The Trakt checkbox only appears with Discovery on and the official Trakt plugin detected, and auto-saves like the Discovery toggle
- DryRun warms discovery caches without persisting, and leaves the shared trending pool untouched
- Greyed-out settings are now truly inert (keyboard and screen readers), and unsaved-changes tracking no longer reports phantom edits
- Tested by 6800 unit tests and 369 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.1.1 - "Trakt for you" no longer stays empty; discovery is quieter and self-healing

- Fixed the main report: "Trakt for you" could stay empty while trending and the local picks were full. Virtual stub library entries (real-looking files with a TMDb id but no media, created by some request helpers) were counted as owned and silently excluded every personal pick. They are now recognised as virtual and ignored, so your Trakt recommendations come through
- An empty "Trakt for you" is no longer sticky: a null or empty result is cached only briefly, so once the server has your picks they appear on the next open instead of being held behind a stale empty view
- A rate-limited or unreachable Trakt is retried with a backoff (honouring the server's Retry-After) instead of being re-hit on every tab load, and the same account open on two devices now shares one fetch instead of firing two
- An unlinked user no longer sees a "Trakt for you" tab that only shows a not-linked message; the tab appears once you are linked, and "Trakt trending" (which needs no login) is always available
- The plugin log now explains an empty personal result in one line (what was fetched, what survived, and why), so a token, fetch, or ownership issue is far easier to pin down
- Tested by 6779 unit tests and 369 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6
- Special thanks to @TheColin21 (https://github.com/TheColin21) for finding and reporting the empty "Trakt for you" issue and for debugging it together ❤️

v3.0.1.0 - Trakt discovery + encrypted secrets, Discovery tab no longer goes blank on Jellyfin 12

- New Trakt discovery source: when the official Jellyfin Trakt plugin is installed, the Discovery tab gains two sub-tabs beside the local picks, "Trakt for you" (your personal Trakt recommendations) and "Trakt trending" (global, no login), using the same card layout, request/dismiss mechanics, and per-user ML scoring. The Helper has no Trakt app of its own: it sources everything read-only through the official plugin's connection, so there is nothing to configure per user and no second app to register. A single "Enable Trakt discovery" checkbox (shown only when the official plugin is detected) turns it on
- All stored credentials (Seerr and Arr API keys) are now encrypted at rest with Data Protection and never logged in plain text; backups stay portable and re-encrypt on restore
- The Seerr Discovery custom tab reliably shows its content again on Jellyfin 12: navigating away and back no longer leaves it blank
- Returning to the tab is instant and never flashes a spinner: the last results render immediately from memory, and newer suggestions are swapped in silently in the background when a scheduled run has produced them
- The sidebar "Seerr Discovery" link opens the tab correctly on the modern Jellyfin 12 layout (both the top header and the narrow-screen menu), as well as on the classic layout
- The Codecs tab cards can now be rearranged by dragging a card's header handle (long-press on touch, with edge auto-scroll) or by keyboard (Enter to grab, arrow keys to move, Enter to drop, Escape to cancel); the order saves instantly, survives refresh/restart/update, and travels with backup export/import
- Radarr/Sonarr instances behind a reverse proxy with a private CA, self-signed, or IP certificate can now connect via a per-instance "Skip certificate validation" checkbox in Settings
- Recommendations now follow completed franchises: a series you finished years ago is surfaced again when a new entry arrives, instead of being outranked by whatever you watched most recently
- Recommendation explanations are now concrete: the "Why" line names what actually drove the pick (completing a collection, a franchise, a matched writer/country/era, or genuine crowd popularity) instead of a vague "Recommended for you". Discovery suggestions keep their person/genre/trending/popularity reasons, now with an honest fallback instead of claiming "Popular and highly rated" for a title that is neither
- Hardening: API keys, the log filter, and backup credentials now reject hidden control characters that could cause errors or log tampering; odd-charset responses are read safely; and restoring a backup that disables TLS validation now warns you first
- Recommendation playlists are always private: playlist sync now sets visibility explicitly instead of relying on the server default, so each user's recommendations stay visible to that user only
- Tested by 6720 unit tests (expanded security, hardening, and performance coverage) and 368 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.2 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6
- Special thanks to @TheColin21 (https://github.com/TheColin21) for testing and donation ❤️
- Special thanks to Daniel for his donation ❤️
- Special thanks to @baervers23 (https://github.com/baervers23) for great input and ideas ❤️

v3.0.0.4 - Per-library file counts, boxset link fix

- The Per-Library Breakdown now shows a file count below every size value (trickplay folders included), so sparse and dense libraries are distinguishable at a glance
- Boxset library rows no longer link into the Library Explorer, whose scope excludes boxsets; they render as plain text instead of opening an empty state
- Every task dropdown in Settings now explains what the task does, via an info button next to each task name, in all dashboard languages
- The Overview Trickplay card now also shows the space used by trickplay images Jellyfin stores internally, on its own line below the alongside-media total, marked with an (internal) badge, or as the headline when no alongside data exists
- Compact log view on phones: log entries stack as cards below 700 px instead of squeezing into a four-column table, so no horizontal scrolling is needed, and rows keep breathing room at the screen edges
- Roomier Library Explorer filter popovers on phones using nearly the full viewport width, like the bitrate editor
- Tested by 6219 unit tests and 352 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.3 - Library Explorer, new Codecs breakdowns, disabled users ignored

- The Codecs tab now has a Library Explorer: combine resolution, codecs, bitrate, languages, watched users and formats into one search, scoped to the libraries you pick in its multi-select, so you can find e.g. all 4K films with low bitrate
- Options with zero matches under the other filters are hidden automatically, dimensions without matches stay greyed out, and multi-value dropdowns accept several audio languages, subtitle languages or users at once
- Every active filter is shown in the result header and a Reset button clears the whole search; results arrive as the familiar grouped file tree with Movies, TV Shows and other sections
- Jump straight into the search from the Overview: each library name and all four media cards open the Explorer pre-filtered to that scope
- Every categorical filter can be negated with Includes/Excludes, so you can search e.g. audio languages that are not German; excluded picks show as ≠ pills and counts preview what stays
- Four new breakdowns in the Codecs tab, each with drill-down to the exact files: Video Bitrate (7 tiers from < 2 to > 60 Mbps), Audio Languages, Subtitle Languages and Watched (by username plus Never watched)
- Each bitrate tier uses what Jellyfin measured for the video stream; when a file has no per-stream value the average is estimated from its size and runtime, so almost every file lands in a real tier instead of Unknown
- Disabled Jellyfin users no longer skew results: their old plays are excluded from Smart Recommendations, watch history and the new Watched breakdown
- Long breakdowns start collapsed behind a Show-all toggle with Unknown always last, and unreadable language tags fold into Unknown instead of junk entries
- Added responsive, independently scrollable library result cards.
- Improved compact layouts for mobile controls.
- Added consistent themed scrollbar styling across plugin panels and lists.
- The Overview Per-Library Breakdown has a new Other column per library covering NFO files, text files and other unrecognized sidecar files, plus a Books column whenever a book library exists, so every row adds up exactly to its Total
- Tested by 6169 unit tests and 341 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.1 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.2 - Log tab, save bar, resolution and touch fixes

- Clearing the plugin log no longer briefly shows a false "Failed to clear logs." error: the Clear button now confirms success immediately and refreshes the view right away
- Genuine clear failures (e.g. expired session or server error) now write a structured diagnostic to the browser console with the HTTP status and error kind, alongside the visible red button feedback, so a real problem is never silent
- Save bar no longer crowds on phones: the unsaved-changes label and Save button now stack on narrow screens, so long translations like the German "Nicht gespeichert" are no longer cut off
- Widescreen films are counted at their real resolution: cinemascope masters like 1920x800 or 1920x1040 are now correctly shown as 1080p instead of 720p in the Codecs tab, decided by whichever axis reaches a resolution class
- The resolution drill-down now lists each file's exact pixel dimensions (e.g. 1920x800) next to its name, readable on desktop and phones
- Chart tooltips work reliably on touch: the first tap on the Trends chart or a Codecs ring now shows and keeps the tooltip instead of flashing it away, and a second tap on the same Codecs segment closes it
- The save confirmation only appears after a real save: reverting a setting back to its original value no longer briefly shows "All changes saved"
- Tested by 5535 unit tests and 320 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.1 - Per-instance library allocation for Arr

- Assign specific Jellyfin libraries to each Radarr/Sonarr instance, so the Arr tab compares an instance only against the libraries it manages
- With two or more instances of a type, each gets a picker in Settings listing only the matching kind of library (movies for Radarr, TV for Sonarr)
- Leave a picker empty to keep it automatic: instances are matched to libraries from their root folders
- Assignments are kept across backup and restore
- Fixes a 4K instance flagging every 1080p film as "not in Radarr"
- Tested by 5499 unit tests and 318 end-to-end tests
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

v3.0.0.0 - Major release for Jellyfin 12.0+

- Books in your library overview: eBook libraries now show their size and file count on the Overview tab and count towards your storage totals, and they're always protected from every cleanup task
- Smarter recommendations: a much bigger model, fairer suggestions for brand-new users, and more variety in your top picks (no more ten near-identical films in a row)
- Recommendations now also learn from franchises/collections, country of origin, collection & folder themes, whether a series is finished or ongoing, writers/creators, top-billed cast, and how rare a genre or studio is in your library (each signal is optional per item, so missing metadata never skews a pick)
- Fresh picks appear between nightly runs, and faster generation on big libraries
- Redesigned Settings, Health and Arr tabs with a live 'reachable' indicator, plus a sticky save bar and unsaved-changes warning
- Better on phones
- Stronger security: API keys are never shown to the browser, backups can leave keys out, and cleanup can never delete or touch anything outside your media libraries
- Safer trash and cleanup: turning retention off really turns it off, trashing a shortcut never removes the file it points to, and Windows shortcut handling is fixed
- More accurate library stats and safer Seerr request cleanup
- More reliable saves and backups (no more rare 'lost save' when antivirus is scanning)
- New end-to-end test suite runs the plugin inside a real Jellyfin 12 server on every change and proves cleanup stays inside your libraries
- Note: your recommendation model retrains from scratch after upgrading, so suggestions settle back in over the next scheduled runs
- Requires Jellyfin 12.0 - if you are on Jellyfin 10.x, stay on v2.1.0.6

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Features
- Frames are no longer taken from inside media segments, so intros, credits, recaps, previews, and commercials stay out of generated artwork
- New Avoid Media Segments setting under Frame Extraction, with a checkbox for each kind of segment to avoid, all on by default
- Segments come from a media segment provider turned on for the library, so items without any extract as before

## Developer
- Changing which segments are avoided discards the idle frame pools, so the next refresh extracts under the new choice

## Features
- New Cleanup Backdrops scheduled task under Library that reduces every item on the server to a single backdrop, keeping the first and deleting the rest along with their files
- The task has no default schedule, so it only runs when started by hand or on a trigger you add

## Features
- Primary and thumb images can name a second and third design, adding their versions of the same frames to the Edit Images picker
- New Edit Images Cache setting for how long rendered choices stay available, default 30 minutes
- Edit Images reuses the choices it already rendered when switching image type or page, instead of rendering every image again

## Fixes
- The Edit Images cache is bounded by size at 256 MB and releases expired images on its own, instead of holding them until the next render
- Every design in one Edit Images render draws from the same frames, even while other items are extracting
- Posters pass over a logo Jellyfin only knows by web address and use the next logo that can be read

## Developer
- Settings saved before 12.0.2.0 are no longer brought forward, so update through 12.0.2.1 first when coming from an older version
- Code, pages, and docs say logo rather than series logo, since films draw their own

## Fixes
- The Profiles page loads again instead of failing on a backdrop setting that no longer exists
- Posters with a logo draw the logo selected for a film, season, or series instead of falling back to text

## Features
- Artwork Generator is Episode Poster Generator rebuilt, with the same settings and a much wider job
- The repository moved with the name; re-add it as jellyfin-plugin-artworkgenerator to keep getting updates
- Draws posters, thumbs, backdrops, and text logos, where before there were only episode posters
- Covers series, seasons, films, music videos, home videos, and anything else with a video
- Configuration is rebuilt in three parts, designs, logos, and profiles
- Profiles decide which items get which images and which design draws each one
- Every design renders portrait and landscape, so one design covers a tall poster and a wide thumb
- A design's two lines are now simply the title and the subtitle, whatever the item is
- Text position and alignment work on every design, not just the few that had them
- New Bloom design, pooling color from the frame behind the text
- New Grid canvas, tiling several extracted frames into one picture
- Logo designs build a text logo from any name field, with letter case, a line limit, and frame-filled letters
- Frame extraction is one set of server settings instead of a copy on every design
- Frames are ranked on tone, detail, contrast, and color rather than just clearing a threshold
- Optional setting drops a subtitle that only repeats the title
- A subtitle too long to fit can shorten to its code, shrink, or trim
- Two example designs per style, each showing a genuinely different look

## Fixes
- Seasons extract from their own episodes instead of falling back to the series backdrop
- Candidate images come from different episodes instead of clustering in one
- Heavily letterboxed frames scale back up to a usable size
- Portrait text is measured against both sides, so it no longer reads small
- Brush strokes stay thick on tall posters instead of piling into a cross
- Long titles trim at a word boundary rather than mid-word
- Descenders stay inside the safe area
- Borders, rules, and shadows scale with the poster
- A static graphic keeps its proportions
- An item with no name of its own says its one line in the larger type
- Generated images carry the item's metadata language

## Developer
- The generator, the settings model, and the configuration page are rebuilt around item kinds rather than episodes
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 that Jellyfin 12.0 ships
- Designs are found by reflection, so adding one needs a class and an enum value
- Every label, option, and default is read from the settings models
- The shared generator is split into pipeline, text, and overlay
- Frame analysis is a single pass, under a megabyte per frame instead of three and a half
- Every one-time upgrade of an older configuration sits in its own file, to be deleted whole once installs have moved on
- Tests hold the documentation, the templates, and US spelling to the code

## Features
- Shadows, rules, and the Frame border now scale with the poster, so they read the same on a 4K frame as on a DVD rip instead of turning into a hairline or a slab
- Long titles that do not fit two lines fill the first line with whole words and trim only the second, at a word boundary, instead of cutting both lines mid-word

## Fixes
- Frame drew no border at all for an episode without a name, and ignored the Show Title setting
- Cutout no longer lets a two line title run into the bottom of the cutout letters
- Split center-crops the series poster into its panel instead of stretching artwork that is not 2:3
- Brush honours the Show Episode setting and keeps a wrapped title inside the area the strokes leave clear
- Timeline keeps the marker dot inside the safe area on the first and last episode
- Text blocks are reserved from the font's real ascent and descent, so descenders no longer hang past the safe area

## Developer
- Built against the SkiaSharp 3.119.4 and Microsoft.Extensions 10.0.11 packages Jellyfin 12.0 ships, since the plugin binds to the server's copies at runtime
- Text drawing moved from the removed SKPaint text members to SKFont, wrapped in a shared TextStyle so every style measures and draws with the same objects
- Standard and Split share one text stack; Numeral, Cutout, Brush, and Frame no longer hand-build their own paints
- Cutout renders through a canvas layer instead of a full-size scratch bitmap per poster; Split and Brush dispose their gradient shaders
- Letterbox detection scans the pixel buffer directly instead of a native call per pixel
- Bitmap scaling uses explicit cubic resampling now that FilterQuality is gone

## Developer
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

## User

## User
- Channels now direct play on clients that support the stream instead of always being remuxed or transcoded by the server

## Developer
- The opened source now sets SupportsDirectPlay. PlaybackInfo always disables direct stream (MediaInfoHelper), so a source that only allowed direct stream could never be picked and every tune-in fell back to DirectPlayError and a remux

## User
- A channel with no viewers now stops when its countdown reaches zero. It used to run on for two to three minutes after the last viewer left
- Tune-in cards are generated for every channel shortly after the server starts and at every guide refresh, including the refresh a save triggers, so a fresh install, an update, a new logo, or changed output settings never leave a channel opening without its card

## Developer
- The linger teardown was vetoed every time because the Jellyfin reader is served right up to the close, so the two-minute recent-delivery rule always saw a viewer at the 30s mark, and the one-shot task then gave up until the reaper backstop 90s plus a minute later. A lingering session now only counts delivery after the close (DeliveryCountsAsWatched, unit tested), and LingerTeardownAsync retries every 5s until the reaper threshold
- LiveChannelsTvService sweeps the tune-in cards 20s after construction and from every GetChannelsAsync (EnsureLogoAsync then IntroService.EnsureAsync per enabled channel, serialised, logged with its trigger); a tune-in without a card now logs it
- The Sessions tab countdown wording no longer uses an em dash or a semicolon

## User
- Tune-in is now immediate. A channel opens on a short animated card (its logo and a Starting Channel caption over flowing lines) the moment you tune in, while the content is seeked and encoded behind it, and the picture no longer waits ten seconds or more for a buffer to fill first
- The Start-up buffer setting is gone. It turned out to be a literal pause Jellyfin applied before every tune-in rather than a buffer, and the cushion it was meant to provide is now built up while you are already watching

## Developer
- Removed StartupBufferSeconds and BufferMs (Jellyfin sleeps for BufferMs in TranscodeManager.AcquireResources before launching the delivery ffmpeg, on every tune-in including adoption)
- The tune-in handover now waits for the playlist and one segment instead of the full cushion, and the endpoint reader's hold-back ramps in one segment per ten seconds of session age instead of applying from the first byte

- Hidden titles show again when they come back on the source or when Removed files leaves Ignore, and a .ignore the plugin did not write is never touched

- The Servers tab says where to add the Whitelist row when the other server refuses this one
- A server running another Server Sync version never overwrites edits recorded here, and changes for it wait in the queue until both match
- An item a peer changed that is announced more than ten times in ten minutes stops being announced, so two servers can never echo a change forever. Deletions always go out

- Playlist edits and deletions are sent as they happen. Pull keeps the parent's copy, Push overrides the other server, and Sync keeps the newest edit
- Playlist sharing and public access are copied when the new Sharing option is on
- Playlist Sync needs a user mapping, and playlists of users without one never leave their server
- Test Connection shows what the key can do on that server, who it belongs to, and whether it may download media
- Test Connection says whether the other server's whitelist lets this key in, and why not
- A standard user's key works for Pull, Push, and Sync, limited to what that user can see and that user's own history, settings, and playlists
- Sync Content skips a server whose key may not download media and logs why
- Check Link reports the access the other server holds for this one
- The sync endpoints only accept administrators from servers on the Servers tab and users on the new Whitelist, each with the locations they may call from
- Whitelist host names are remembered and looked up again when a caller stops matching, so dynamic DNS keeps working
- Refused sync calls are logged with the user, the address, and the reason
- Servers that pull from this one without being on its Servers tab need a Whitelist row after updating
- The plugin's endpoints moved from /ServerSync to /Sync
- Every sync type in Settings shows what a standard user and an administrator can do
- Settings descriptions are shorter, and retries, approvals, and download speed are tables
- Settings groups the sync types under Synchronization
- User Sync and History Sync only use the key's own user when the key is a standard user's
- The new Permissions page in the docs lists what each function needs
- Identify lists every server that has the item, in the Servers tab order, and picking one keeps the item on that server
- The image picker shows the images of every server that has the item, each named after its server
- Log entries strip control characters from values another server sends

## Developer
- Activity entries for changes sent again, paused peers, and rejected requests name the items involved and say why
- Activity entry details start with a capital letter
- Metadata provider image previews load from the server's External URL when one is set, so a server reached at an internal address still shows them

## Developer
- The metadata provider matches by the item's provider ids when the file path does not match, and seasons and episodes by the show's ids with their season and episode numbers
- The metadata provider logs why it found no match for an item
- A server that could not be reached or runs another version is asked again after 30 seconds

## Developer
- Every server in a pool must run the same Server Sync version. Calls from another version are refused, and Check Link names both versions. Update every server together
- Hints are answered with a code that says what the receiver did with them
- Each server tells the others what it wants from them, so changes outside its mapped libraries, users, and filters are never sent
- A change the other server turned away is held back from it for a day, or until the settings on either side change
- A hint for an item a server does not have yet waits up to seven days and applies when the item arrives. The queue view shows these as waiting for the item
- A server that already holds the same or a newer edit answers straight away without fetching anything
- Server Sync is a metadata and image provider for every media type. Enable it in a library's metadata and image fetchers to fill new items from the servers it pulls from
- Content and Metadata scans read only what changed on each server. A full scan runs every 24 hours, set by Full Scan Every under Processing
- Peer status reads need the asking server's id and its pairing
- Removed unused API routes

## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## Developer
- A hint is applied only when the item's own path on the origin is inside a mapped library, not just the path the hint names
- Server Sync does not follow redirects from another server. A redirect is reported with the address to use instead

- Any signed in user's key can pair, so a peer held with a standard user's key pairs like any other
- A peer that cannot pair has its hints refused instead of being taken on its word
- When one server holds a standard user's key for the other, both need this version to pair

## Developer
- Only changes to items in a mapped library, and watch history for mapped users, are queued for a peer. Everything else is dropped before it gathers, so it is never checked or sent

## Developer
- The Queue view's warning about local changes that matched no mapping has a Dismiss button, and saving the configuration checks those changes again so a newly mapped library or user sends them
- Processing settings set how hints are retried. A peer that cannot be reached is tried again after 30 seconds, doubling up to an hour, and a peer that refuses waits 15 minutes. Each has a max retries setting, where 0 keeps trying forever
- The Sync page opens on the Queue when no sync module is enabled, instead of an empty page

## Developer
- Built on base 2026.10.6, which now owns the database's schema version, its oldest reader marker, and setting an unreadable database aside
- A database set aside because a newer version wrote it is kept as a .newer backup instead of a .corrupt one, and the three newest of each are kept
- Activity log entries are written through the base package's logger

## Developer
- The five Sync tables are built from one shared module, so a fix to the table, its buttons, or its modals reaches every view at once
- The refresh run is split into named steps, with the prune's safety checks gathered in one place
- Every Sync view reloads its counts and health figures when a detail dialog closes, and alerts and empty states read the same across views

## Developer
- A slow or silent peer no longer stops hint delivery until a restart. Peer calls have a deadline that covers the whole answer, connections time out after fifteen seconds, and peers are served in parallel
- Two servers holding the same version with different values settle instead of trading the hint forever, and a server only announces edits it made itself
- A sender whose clock runs a few minutes ahead sees its hints completed instead of resent forever
- Versions only move forward, are written at the moment of a hand made edit, and a scan records the version it read with each value rather than asking the peer again per row
- A failed version read no longer lets a scan overwrite edits made here, and those rows wait for the next scan
- In a pool of three or more, a history base made stale by a third server no longer reverts a newer edit, and both sides record a base when nothing needed to change
- Jellyfin's own housekeeping saves no longer pose as hand made edits, and provider work never replaces an item locked here
- Content hints obey the library's allow and block lists and the watched by all filter, and a downloaded file is no longer announced back to the pool
- The negotiated history base cannot be rolled back by a scan, and moving rows to a higher priority server keeps ignored rows and bases and counts toward the safety limit, judged per server like the prune
- The hidden per module tasks no longer run on schedules of their own
- Removing a server takes effect only once saved, removes the hints it sent, and a slow answer for one server can no longer land in another server's editor
- The stored key and pairing secret are only sent to the address saved on the entry, and IPv4 addresses written as IPv6 are checked as IPv4
- Hint queues are bounded and indexed. A full inbound queue answers busy, hints give up after about a day, sent and failed rows expire after a week, and errored rows are retried daily
- A scheduled run no longer holds hint applies for its whole length, and a backlog drains without waiting between batches
- The Queue view refreshes only when something changed, caches posters, shows at most 200 rows, and resumes refreshing when you come back to the page
- A timeout on one item no longer aborts a whole scheduled run, one server that fails to list no longer stops the others, and one module that fails no longer skips the rest of Sync Information or Sync Content
- A transient error no longer reads as an item, a library page, or a profile image being gone, so it cannot truncate a scan or clear a user's picture
- Replacing a file keeps its NFO, images, and other sidecars, a renamed file on a source is moved instead of downloaded again, and a file still on disk stays tracked when its source item goes
- Free space is measured on the library's own disk, the sign in honors the private network rule, and the address check refuses unspecified and multicast addresses
- Retry errors works for History, Metadata, People, and Users, the dashboard keeps scrolling and refreshing after you come back, and slow answers no longer land in the wrong server or modal
- The database records the oldest version that can read it, so going back to an older version keeps it whenever that version can read it
- Every stored and compared time is read and written as UTC in one place
- Writing an item's cast holds back people hints only during the write, not while its images download
- The sync table shows deletions held for approval and deletions in progress when deletion is set to Enabled
- A hint that could not apply shows as Skipped sync for its name on the Activity page, with a plainer reason when the person does not exist here
- Dead code removed and repeated code shared across the plugin, with docs corrected where they had drifted

## Developer
- A season names its series in the activity log and the queue, as Synced The Show Season 1, instead of Season 1 alone

## Developer
- A peer's version can no longer lie ahead of this server's clock. A hint dated more than five minutes ahead is declined, anything less is read as now, and the version store never holds a future stamp
- Requests that name a sender must prove it. Each server issues the servers it lists a pairing secret over its own connection to them, and a batch, completion, or history negotiation without the right secret answers 428 until the real server pairs, which Check Link and the workers do on their own. A server held with a standard user's key cannot be issued one and is taken on its word, as before
- A completion removes only the reporting peer's own rows
- An entry that disallows private networks now holds a name to the same rule as an address, at save time and on every connection
- The inbound queue keeps at most ten thousand rows per origin, finished ids are capped, and a peer's answer is read up to thirty two megabytes
- Nothing gathers or shows for a kind no Push or Sync server applies, though a hand made edit still records its version, and the ancestor walk that sorts provider images from edits runs only when it decides anything
- An applied episode logs Synced [series] S01E02 with [type] [series] S01E02 - [episode] was updated from [server], activity entries no longer end in a full stop, and provider work applied from a peer's scan writes none
- A pass of metadata hints reads the origin's items in pages of fifty, as the scheduled scan does, instead of one request per hint
- The Queue view shows episodes and videos in a wide frame, and its count cards wrap three then two on a phone

## Developer
- An applied change writes Synced [name]. to the activity log, with [type] [name] was updated from [server]. as the detail
- The duplicate DELETE /ServerSync/Peer/Queue/{id} route is gone. Every route requires an administrator, which a unit test and the integration suite now enforce
- The Queue view is one list. Each change is one row for its whole life with a status chip, Jellyfin's title and poster, the user for watch history, a ticking countdown while it gathers, the summary cards and peers as filters, and a layout that stacks on phones

## Developer
- Every metadata and image change travels, posters included. Provider work from a scan or a refresh is marked, fills in where the other server has recorded no edit, and never replaces a poster or field set by hand. Sync database schema v26
- The Queue view lists the changes still gathering, named, with when each goes out, and its To Send card is now Pending
- An applied change writes [type] [name] was updated to the activity log, with the peer it was triggered from in the detail
- User settings are no longer announced live, since Jellyfin raises no event for policy and configuration changes. The scheduled Sync Information task carries them, and the Users settings say so
- Check Link reads as plain sentences

## Developer
- A server only announces the kinds of change its peer applies, read from the peer's enabled modules every minute; Check Link and each peer's card on the Queue view name them
- Send Changes After, under Settings > Processing, sets how long an item must go untouched before a change is sent to peers, sixty seconds by default; every further edit restarts the wait and one update goes out at the end of it
- History hints honour the receiver's History switch like every other kind
- New library mapping rows start enabled
- The Queue view says when a local change matched no library or user mapping on any Push or Sync server, and names the last one
- A poster or other image uploaded or picked by hand travels as a metadata hint; images a provider fetches during a scan or a refresh are still left to the scheduled task

## Developer
- Targets Jellyfin 12.1
- Several servers, scanned in priority order. The single source migrates into the list
- Server modes Pull, Push, and Sync. Push and Sync send change hints to peers running Server Sync, which pull each change within seconds
- Hints cover watch history, metadata, people, users, and new files. Stored on both ends, retried with backoff, recovered when lost
- Watch history merges three way against the state both servers last agreed on
- Metadata, people, and users resolve on where and when a value was last edited, so the newest edit wins
- Two scheduled tasks, Sync Content and Sync Information, replace the ten. The per module tasks are hidden but still run from the dashboard
- Peer endpoints under /ServerSync/Peer and operator endpoints under /ServerSync/Hints, all behind Jellyfin's RequiresElevation policy
- {'Servers tab rebuilt': 'numbered priority list with reorder, Connection, Authentication, Libraries, and Users steps, API key or sign in, and Check Link judged by direction with a clock skew warning'}
- A standard user's key is recognised and pulls what that user can see, one way
- Queue view on the Sync page, and an activity log line for every concluded hint
- A full REST API section in the README
- Each detail dialog shows which server last edited the item and when
- Removing a server removes the rows tracked from it
- Pending hints capped at ten thousand per peer
- Server names with emoji work in peer requests

## Developer
- Items with several backdrops no longer queue on every refresh. Jellyfin stores images without an order, so the same set can come back shuffled on either server. Image sizes are now matched as a set within each image type instead of by position
- Metadata Sync people no longer queue again right after a successful sync. Credits are compared the way Jellyfin stores them, ignoring case and padding on names and roles and collapsing duplicate credits, and the post apply check uses the same comparison as the refresh

description:
Create smart, rule-based playlists and collections in Jellyfin — for movies, shows, music, or anything your library holds. A single genre rule takes seconds; stack rules into groups and you can express almost anything. Either way, they keep themselves up to date.
